title: Understanding the Model
text: Rohan's model is given by \( \hat{y}_i=\theta\log(x_i**{2}) \). This means that for each data point \( $$x_i$$ \), the predicted value \( \hat{y}_i \) is a linear function of \( \log(x_i**{2}) \).

title: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
text: The Mean Squared Error (MSE) is defined as \( \frac{1}{n}\sum{i\=1}{n}{(y_i-\hat{y}_i)**{2}} \). To minimize this, we need to find the value of \( $$\theta$$ \) that minimizes the sum of squared differences between the actual \( $$y_i$$ \) and predicted \( \hat{y}_i \).

title: Simplifying the Expression
text: Substitute \( \hat{y}_i=\theta\log(x_i**{2}) \) into the MSE formula. This gives \( \frac{1}{n}\sum{i\=1}{n}{(y_i-\theta\log(x_i**{2}))**{2}} \).

title: Taking the Derivative
text: To find the value of \( $$\theta$$ \) that minimizes the MSE, take the derivative of the MSE with respect to \( $$\theta$$ \) and set it to zero. This will give you the optimal \( \hat{\theta} \).
